record.narrative: I interpreted all new evidence using the registered signed convention: for direction -1, a positive signed value means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive signed value means weaker dependency in the exposed group; for interactions, a positive signed value means modification in the claimed interaction direction. The central predictor map remains unchanged and strong: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency, while TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are associated with much weaker dependency, and MSI-high status is associated with much stronger dependency. These are dataset-specific measured associations, not causal or externally generalizable claims.  PTEN loss remains the key unresolved secondary predictor. H108 tests PTEN loss among STK11-intact cells and gives a signed mean difference of +0.205 (95% interval +0.097 to +0.312). The point estimate is threshold-sized, but the interval lower bound is well below the 0.15-unit threshold, so I keep it unresolved and active rather than accept it. H111 tests PTEN loss among STK11-intact TP53-intact cells and is the most suggestive new PTEN result: +0.235, interval +0.136 to +0.334. The point estimate is robustly above threshold, but the lower bound is still slightly below threshold and this is one of many correlated PTEN context tests. I therefore keep H111 unresolved but active because it is the most promising lower-mask PTEN context pending independent validation. H110 tests PTEN loss among STK11-intact adenocarcinoma cells and gives +0.179, interval +0.052 to +0.306. It is positive but too imprecise to support a threshold-sized conclusion; I mark it unresolved and deferred. H112 directly tests whether STK11 loss attenuates the PTEN-loss contrast in the claimed direction. The signed interaction is -0.118, interval -0.360 to +0.124, so there is no supported threshold-sized attenuation; I reject and close it.  H109 asks whether the broad MSI-high stronger-dependency association persists in adenocarcinoma. The signed estimate is +0.742, interval +0.605 to +0.878, far above threshold. I accept and close H109. This is consistent with the already validated broad MSI-high effect and supports that the signal is not driven only by the minority non-adenocarcinoma cells, but it remains a dataset-specific association.  Growth-rate interactions did not support the registered hypotheses. H113, SMARCA4-loss amplification in faster-growing cells, has signed estimate -0.136, interval -0.286 to +0.015; it is not in the claimed positive direction and is not threshold-sized. H114, TP53-loss attenuation in faster-growing cells, has signed estimate -0.107, interval -0.320 to +0.107. H115, KEAP1-loss attenuation in faster-growing cells, has signed estimate +0.097, interval -0.046 to +0.241. None provide robust evidence of a threshold-sized modification, so I reject and close all three. These rejections indicate lack of supported evidence in this dataset, not proof that the true interaction is exactly zero.  The remaining PTEN transcriptomic interactions were also unsupported. H74, PTEN loss by MYC expression state, is near null: -0.003, interval -0.182 to +0.177. H75, PTEN loss by high Wnt activity, has estimate +0.145, interval -0.035 to +0.324; the point is near threshold but the interval includes zero and the point is not robustly threshold-sized, so I reject and close. H79, STK11 loss by hypoxia state, has estimate +0.060, interval -0.094 to +0.215, and is unsupported. The batch diagnostic H116 is also unsupported: batch_a versus batch_b has signed estimate -0.011, interval -0.096 to +0.073. This does not rule out all batch-related variation, but it does not support a threshold-sized difference for this particular batch contrast.  The most informative next independent validation target is broad PTEN loss, H32. Several PTEN contexts are already accepted, but the whole-population PTEN claim remains unresolved because its discovery lower bound, +0.131, is just below the 0.15 threshold while the point estimate is +0.227. Independent validation of H32 directly tests whether PTEN loss should be described as a broadly supported secondary association or only as a collection of context-specific localizations. I therefore request validation of H32 and keep broad PTEN, H108, and H111 active while deferring lower-priority PTEN context and exploratory interaction leads.

The four core validated associations remain dataset-specific associations only: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency_composite, TP53 loss with much weaker dependency, KEAP1 loss with much weaker dependency, and MSI-high status with much stronger dependency. Under the signed convention used for these proposals, for main-effect claims with direction -1 a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has stronger dependency, whereas for direction +1 a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has weaker dependency. For interactions, a positive signed estimate means the raw subgroup-minus-complement contrast is in the registered interaction direction.\n\nFirst, PTEN loss remains the most important unresolved secondary predictor. The broad PTEN claim H32 has a positive point estimate but a 95% lower bound below the 0.15-unit threshold, while several restricted PTEN contexts have already been accepted, including TP53-intact cells, KEAP1-intact cells, triple-intact molecular backgrounds, and KEAP1-loss/TP53-intact cells. The active untested claim H108 tests PTEN loss broadly among STK11-intact cells. I therefore propose two principled PTEN refinements: PTEN loss among STK11-intact adenocarcinoma cells and PTEN loss among STK11-intact TP53-intact cells. These are not arbitrary context fishing; they test whether the unresolved broad PTEN signal is diluted by rare histology, STK11-loss co-mutations, or TP53-loss co-mutations. The first combines a common histological population with STK11-intact status, refining the deferred adenocarcinoma PTEN claim. The second combines two low-mask backgrounds already relevant to accepted PTEN contexts. I also register a direct PTEN-by-STK11 interaction, with direction +1, to test whether the PTEN-loss contrast is less negative in STK11-loss cells than in STK11-intact cells. Because H97/H101 show positive but underpowered PTEN estimates within STK11-loss backgrounds while STK11-intact PTEN remains untested, the modification direction is uncertain; this interaction is useful as a falsifier rather than as a strong prediction.\n\nSecond, I propose growth-rate interactions for three core predictors using the median growth_rate_doublings_per_day split. record.narrative: This synthesis resolves the pending validation responses and refines the interpretation of PTEN loss. Under the signed convention, for direction -1 a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has stronger dependency, and for direction +1 a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has weaker dependency; for interactions, a positive signed estimate means modification in the claimed interaction direction. H14, KEAP1 loss with direction +1, is independently confirmed: discovery signed mean difference +0.832 (95% interval +0.766 to +0.897) and independent validation +0.765 (adjusted interval +0.669 to +0.861). The validation lower bound is far above the 0.15-unit threshold, so I accept and close H14. KEAP1 loss is associated with substantially weaker dependency_composite in this dataset, without causal or external-generalizability claims. H32, broad PTEN loss with direction -1, remains not robustly confirmed. Discovery gives +0.227 (95% interval +0.131 to +0.323) and independent validation gives +0.200 (adjusted interval +0.048 to +0.351). Both point estimates exceed 0.15 and are concordant with several accepted PTEN context-specific claims, but neither the original 95% lower bound nor the conservative independent validation lower bound excludes threshold-or-smaller effects. I therefore keep H32 unresolved and defer it as a suggestive whole-population association rather than accept broad PTEN as a robust threshold-sized effect. The supported dataset-specific predictor map remains: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency (H5), TP53 loss with much weaker dependency (H13), KEAP1 loss with much weaker dependency (H14), and MSI-high status with much stronger dependency (H80, including H109 in adenocarcinoma). PTEN loss is supported as a secondary predictor in multiple measured backgrounds, including TP53-intact cells (H39), KEAP1-intact cells (H40), triple-intact TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4 backgrounds (H33), KEAP1-loss TP53-intact backgrounds (H51/H102), TP53/KEAP1-intact backgrounds (H58), TP53/SMARCA4-intact backgrounds (H91), and an adenocarcinoma low-mask background (H103), but the broad unadjusted PTEN claim is still best described as suggestive and context-dependent. Negative findings include broad lack of robust support for KRAS mutation, STK11 loss overall, MYC amplification, PIK3CA mutation, ARID1A loss, MTAP loss, RB1 loss, SMAD4 loss, research markers D/E/F, APC mutation, NF1 loss, BRCA2 loss, BRAF mutation, EGFR amplification, ERBB2 amplification, omics-availability indicators, CRISPR library indicators, media-serum level, and the batch_a versus batch_b diagnostic. Most tested interactions, including lineage-subtype, growth-rate, mutation-burden, MYC-expression, Wnt-activity, hypoxia, and several co-mutation interactions, did not provide robust threshold-sized evidence, although some remain underpowered rather than definitively absent. Main unresolved uncertainties are broad PTEN H32, PTEN in STK11-intact and STK11-intact TP53-intact backgrounds H108/H111, PTEN in STK11-loss backgrounds H97/H101, the TP53-by-STK11 interaction H105, small-sample MSI-high contexts H94/H95, and the untested exploratory interaction panel H76-H78. The most informative next analysis is independent validation of H111, PTEN loss among STK11-intact TP53-intact cells, because it has the most promising unresolved PTEN signal with adequate sample size. If H111 validates with a lower bound above 0.15, PTEN can be upgraded from highly context-specific to a broader secondary predictor in common backgrounds; if not, the PTEN conclusion should remain restricted to already accepted contexts and H32/H108/H110 should remain suggestive only. All statements remain associations in this supplied dataset, not causal mechanisms or externally generalizable rules.

prompt:
Iteration 10/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

PTEN loss among adenocarcinoma cells that are KEAP1-intact and TP53-intact tests whether the common low-mask background suggested by accepted PTEN effects can yield a threshold-sized estimate; alternatives are that the signal remains diluted or that the estimate is only context-specific. PTEN loss among SMARCA4-loss TP53-intact cells tests whether the huge SMARCA4-loss association masks a secondary PTEN effect; the prior PTEN-by-SMARCA4 interaction was not supported, but a direct conditional main effect remains scientifically useful as a masking/falsification test. PTEN loss among high mutation-burden cells tests whether the broad PTEN point estimate is concentrated in high-TMB backgrounds, which may include MSI-high co-occurrence; if supported, that supports broader PTEN relevance but should be interpreted cautiously because MSI-high is itself a strong accepted predictor. Second, I propose quality-screen interactions for the three core genomic predictors: SMARCA4 loss, KEAP1 loss, and TP53 loss, split at median screen_roc_auc. These are diagnostic rather than mechanistic hypotheses. A threshold-sized interaction in the predicted direction would support that the core associations are stronger in better-quality screens; a null result would support the reliability of the accepted map in this dataset; a threshold-sized attenuation would indicate potential technical dependence. Third, I register a biologically coherent secondary follow-up for CDKN2A loss: testing whether the CDKN2A-loss association is amplified in cells with low copy number at 9p21. CDKN2A loss was only near threshold overall and remains unresolved in several contexts, so a deletion-context interaction is a focused test of biologically meaningful amplification rather than arbitrary subgroup fishing. The next appraise should still prioritize independent validation of H111, PTEN loss in STK11-intact TP53-intact cells, because that is currently the most informative unresolved PTEN context and should decide whether PTEN is upgraded toward broader secondary relevance or kept restricted. If H111 validates, many new PTEN contexts can be treated as supportive consolidation; if it fails, accepted PTEN contexts should remain narrow and the new PTEN proposals should be assessed as context tests rather than as a reason to accept broad PTEN. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Under the signed convention used here, for main effects with direction -1 a positive signed value means stronger dependency in the exposed group, while for direction +1 a positive signed value means weaker dependency; for interactions, a positive signed value means the subgroup-minus-complement contrast is stronger in the registered interaction direction. First, I propose three new PTEN-loss contexts that test different explanations for why broad PTEN loss remains unresolved. PTEN loss among adenocarcinoma cells that are KEAP1-intact and TP53-intact tests whether the common low-mask background suggested by accepted PTEN effects can yield a threshold-sized estimate; alternatives are that the signal remains diluted or that the estimate is only context-specific. PTEN loss among SMARCA4-loss TP53-intact cells tests whether the huge SMARCA4-loss association masks a secondary PTEN effect; the prior PTEN-by-SMARCA4 interaction was not supported, but a direct conditional main effect remains scientifically useful as a masking/falsification test. PTEN loss among high mutation-burden cells tests whether the broad PTEN point estimate is concentrated in high-TMB backgrounds, which may include MSI-high co-occurrence; if supported, that supports broader PTEN relevance but should be interpreted cautiously because MSI-high is itself a strong accepted predictor. Second, I propose quality-screen interactions for the three core genomic predictors: SMARCA4 loss, KEAP1 loss, and TP53 loss, split at median screen_roc_auc. These are diagnostic rather than mechanistic hypotheses. A threshold-sized interaction in the predicted direction would support that the core associations are stronger in better-quality screens; a null result would support the reliability of the accepted map in this dataset; a threshold-sized attenuation would indicate potential technical dependence. Third, I register a biologically coherent secondary follow-up for CDKN2A loss: testing whether the CDKN2A-loss association is amplified in cells with low copy number at 9p21. CDKN2A loss was only near threshold overall and remains unresolved in several contexts, so a deletion-context interaction is a focused test of biologically meaningful amplification rather than arbitrary subgroup fishing. The highest-priority group is PTEN-loss breadth and masking: H117 tests PTEN loss in adenocarcinoma cells that are KEAP1-intact and TP53-intact, a common low-mask context that could strengthen or narrow the secondary PTEN interpretation; H118 tests PTEN loss among SMARCA4-loss TP53-intact cells, asking whether PTEN remains associated after the very large SMARCA4-loss association; and H119 tests PTEN loss among high mutation-burden cells, which may reveal whether broad PTEN effects are concentrated in high-TMB backgrounds but must be interpreted cautiously because MSI-high is a strong accepted predictor. Next, H120-H122 test screen-quality robustness of the core map using median screen_roc_auc splits for SMARCA4 loss, KEAP1 loss, and TP53 loss; these are diagnostic rather than mechanistic and could support that the accepted associations are not diluted in lower-quality screens. Iteration 10/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

Iteration 10/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: This synthesis evaluates the three pending evidence deadlines and updates the dataset-specific conclusion about PTEN loss. All numbers below are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction: for main effects with direction -1, a positive estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive estimate means weaker dependency. H40 tests PTEN loss among KEAP1-intact cells in the stronger-dependency direction. Discovery gave +0.233 (95% interval +0.133 to +0.332; R35), and independent validation gave a larger adjusted estimate +0.328 with adjusted lower bound +0.184 (R105). Because the point estimate and the independent validation lower bound both exceed the 0.15-unit threshold, I accept and close H40. This provides a robust, dataset-specific association between PTEN loss and stronger dependency in the KEAP1-intact background, without claiming causality or external generalizability. H46 tests EGFR amplification in the weaker-dependency direction. Discovery gave a small and imprecise +0.092 (-0.014 to +0.197; R60), and independent validation gave +0.036 (-0.102 to +0.174; R106). The validation estimate is far below threshold and the adjusted interval is incompatible with a threshold-sized effect. I therefore reject and close H46 as unsupported: EGFR amplification is not a meaningful positive predictor of weaker dependency_composite in this supplied dataset. H111 tests PTEN loss among cells that are STK11-intact and TP53-intact, the main unresolved broad-context PTEN hypothesis. Discovery gave +0.235 with lower bound +0.136 (R109), and independent validation gave +0.263 with adjusted lower bound +0.105 (R130). The direction is concordant and both point estimates are above the threshold, but neither interval provides a lower bound above the 0.15-unit threshold; in particular, the independent validation interval remains compatible with a smaller-than-threshold effect. Therefore I keep H111 unresolved and deferred rather than accept it. This failure of independent interval confirmation is important: it argues against upgrading PTEN loss to a broad, uniformly threshold-sized secondary predictor in common low-mask backgrounds. It does not overturn the already accepted context-specific PTEN associations, because those contexts have their own discovery or validation evidence, but it supports interpreting PTEN loss as a context-dependent secondary predictor rather than a broadly robust main effect. The current supported dataset-specific map remains: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency_composite (H5 and related accepted contexts), TP53 loss with much weaker dependency_composite (H13 and related accepted contexts), KEAP1 loss with much weaker dependency_composite (H14 and related accepted contexts), and MSI-high status with much stronger dependency_composite (H80 and related accepted contexts, including adenocarcinoma-restricted H109). PTEN loss is supported as a secondary association in several measured backgrounds, including TP53-intact cells, KEAP1-intact cells, TP53/KEAP1-intact cells, TP53/SMARCA4-intact cells, triple-intact TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4 cells, KEAP1-loss TP53-intact cells, and an adenocarcinoma TP53/SMARCA4-intact background. The broad unadjusted PTEN claim remains suggestive but not robust, because H32 and several lower-confidence PTEN context claims have lower confidence bounds at or below the threshold. Negative findings are broad: KRAS mutation, STK11 loss overall, MYC amplification, PIK3CA mutation, ARID1A loss, MTAP loss, RB1 loss, SMAD4 loss, NF1 loss, BRCA2 loss, BRAF mutation, EGFR amplification including independent validation, ERBB2 amplification, APC mutation, research markers D/E/F, omics-availability indicators, CRISPR library indicators, media-serum level, and batch_a versus batch_b diagnostics did not show robust threshold-sized associations in the claimed direction. Most tested interactions were also unsupported or insufficient, including lineage-subtype, growth-rate, mutation-burden, screen-quality, Wnt-activity, aneuploidy, low-9p21, hypoxia, stemness, and MYC-expression context tests. Some negative conclusions are absence of evidence rather than proof of exact nullity, especially in small cells. Remaining unresolved issues include broad PTEN loss, PTEN in STK11-intact backgrounds including H108/H110/H111/H117-H119, PTEN in STK11-loss backgrounds H97/H101, selected CDKN2A contexts, TP53-by-STK11 interaction H105, small-sample MSI-high subgroups, and exploratory interactions such as H78. Given the failed H111 validation, the most informative next analysis is not another broad PTEN claim. If the remaining voluntary validation request is used, it is better spent on a well-powered accepted or near-accepted low-mask PTEN context such as H58, PTEN loss in TP53-intact KEAP1-intact cells, or H33, PTEN loss in triple-intact TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4 cells, to strengthen the contextual PTEN map. Otherwise, a focused follow-up on PTEN in STK11-loss backgrounds H97/H101 or a pre-specified aggregation of low-mask contexts would be more useful than accepting H32 or H111. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal mechanisms or externally generalizable rules.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

First, I propose three new PTEN-loss contexts that test different explanations for why broad PTEN loss remains unresolved. PTEN loss among adenocarcinoma cells that are KEAP1-intact and TP53-intact tests whether the common low-mask background suggested by accepted PTEN effects can yield a threshold-sized estimate; alternatives are that the signal remains diluted or that the estimate is only context-specific. These are diagnostic rather than mechanistic hypotheses. A threshold-sized interaction in the predicted direction would support that the core associations are stronger in better-quality screens; a null result would support the reliability of the accepted map in this dataset; a threshold-sized attenuation would indicate potential technical dependence. Iteration 11/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

PTEN loss remains the main unresolved secondary predictor: broad PTEN and several common-context PTEN estimates have confidence bounds that do not clearly exceed the 0.15-unit threshold, and failed independent interval confirmation for H111 argues against treating PTEN as a uniformly broad threshold-sized effect. PTEN should be interpreted as context-dependent unless a focused, well-powered low-mask context validates. Proposed new comparisons serve three purposes: (1) PTEN excluding MSI-high tests whether PTEN loss retains a threshold-sized stronger-dependency association when the strong MSI-high predictor is removed; if PTEN is confounded by or concentrated with MSI-high, the non-MSI estimate should attenuate. (2) A low-TMB non-MSI PTEN test is a stricter pre-specified context check against broad PTEN relevance. (3) A PTEN-by-aneuploidy interaction tests whether PTEN association is modified by chromosomal-instability background, with the anticipated direction being stronger dependency in high aneuploidy but alternatives including null or opposite modification. The MYC-by-8q24 interaction tests whether MYC-amplification effects are genomically coherent with the MYC locus; MYC amplification as a binary variable is unsupported overall, so this is a focused locus-aware follow-up. Cas9-activity and adherent-growth-pattern interactions are technical robustness checks for the three strongest genomic associations: SMARCA4, KEAP1, and TP53. A threshold-sized interaction in the expected direction would indicate that these associations are concentrated in higher editing/adherent settings; a null interaction supports reliability in the supplied dataset; an opposite threshold-sized attenuation would indicate potential technical dependence. First, I propose PTEN-loss comparisons that directly interrogate the unresolved broad PTEN signal. PTEN loss among MSI-high-negative cells is a confounding/focus test: MSI-high is already a very strong accepted stronger-dependency predictor, so if PTEN loss is merely a partial marker of MSI-high biology, the non-MSI PTEN estimate should shrink toward null. A threshold-sized result would strengthen the case for PTEN as a context-independent secondary association in non-MSI backgrounds, but a lower confidence bound below 0.15 would support keeping PTEN narrowly context-specific. The second PTEN proposal tests whether PTEN association is modified by aneuploidy. If chromosomal instability amplifies or co-occurs with PTEN-loss dependency effects, the raw interaction should be more negative in high-aneuploidy cells; the alternative is null or opposite modification, which would weaken PTEN's contextual coherence. A third PTEN proposal tests the low-mutation-burden non-MSI context, a stricter low-TMB, low-MSI background that can determine whether PTEN effects survive after removing both high mutation burden and MSI-high backgrounds. Second, I propose a locus-aware MYC test. MYC amplification as a binary variable was not supported, but its genomic concordance with 8q24 copy gain remains scientifically plausible; if MYC-amplification dependency effects are more negative in high 8q24 copy-number contexts, that supports a biologically meaningful amplification-context effect. A null interaction supports treating MYC amplification as not threshold-sized in this dataset. Third, I propose technical robustness interactions for the three strongest accepted predictors. High Cas9 activity and adherent growth pattern are diagnostic moderators. For SMARCA4 loss, the expected direction for stronger dependency is more negative in the subgroup; for KEAP1 and TP53 loss, the expected direction for weaker dependency is more positive in the subgroup. These are not mechanistic claims: a threshold-sized interaction would indicate that the core associations are concentrated in particular assay conditions, while a null interaction supports that the accepted core map is not strongly diluted by these measured technical/contextual features in the supplied dataset. record.narrative: I selected the 10 currently untested registered claims H124-H133; these are all active empty-evidence claims, so they can yield new discovery results. Previously tested claims were avoided because rerunning them gives no new sample. The batch prioritizes PTEN context: H124 tests PTEN loss excluding MSI-high to assess whether the secondary PTEN signal survives when the very strong MSI-high predictor is removed, while H133 tests a stricter low-mutation-burden non-MSI background. H125 tests whether PTEN-loss dependency effects are modified by chromosomal instability. H126 is a locus-aware follow-up to unsupported MYC amplification, testing whether MYC-amplification effects are more consistent with a claimed stronger-dependency direction in high 8q24 copy-number backgrounds. The remaining six are diagnostic moderators of the accepted core map: high Cas9 activity (H127-H129) and adherent growth pattern (H130-H132) for SMARCA4 loss, KEAP1 loss, and TP53 loss. For direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates support stronger dependency in the exposed group or claimed amplification of the effect in the subgroup; for direction +1 claims, positive signed estimates support weaker dependency in the exposed group or claimed amplification in the subgroup. Interpretation will require effect magnitude and uncertainty around the 0.15-unit threshold, not just interval exclusion of zero.

prompt:
Iteration 11/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

All estimates requested will be signed to the registered direction, so for main effects with direction -1 a positive signed estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed group, whereas for direction +1 a positive signed estimate supports weaker dependency. First, I propose PTEN-loss comparisons that directly interrogate the unresolved broad PTEN signal. PTEN loss among MSI-high-negative cells is a confounding/focus test: MSI-high is already a very strong accepted stronger-dependency predictor, so if PTEN loss is merely a partial marker of MSI-high biology, the non-MSI PTEN estimate should shrink toward null. A threshold-sized result would strengthen the case for PTEN as a context-independent secondary association in non-MSI backgrounds, but a lower confidence bound below 0.15 would support keeping PTEN narrowly context-specific. The second PTEN proposal tests whether PTEN association is modified by aneuploidy. If chromosomal instability amplifies or co-occurs with PTEN-loss dependency effects, the raw interaction should be more negative in high-aneuploidy cells; the alternative is null or opposite modification, which would weaken PTEN's contextual coherence. A third PTEN proposal tests the low-mutation-burden non-MSI context, a stricter low-TMB, low-MSI background that can determine whether PTEN effects survive after removing both high mutation burden and MSI-high backgrounds. Second, I propose a locus-aware MYC test. MYC amplification as a binary variable was not supported, but its genomic concordance with 8q24 copy gain remains scientifically plausible; if MYC-amplification dependency effects are more negative in high 8q24 copy-number contexts, that supports a biologically meaningful amplification-context effect. A null interaction supports treating MYC amplification as not threshold-sized in this dataset. Third, I propose technical robustness interactions for the three strongest accepted predictors. High Cas9 activity and adherent growth pattern are diagnostic moderators. For SMARCA4 loss, the expected direction for stronger dependency is more negative in the subgroup; for KEAP1 and TP53 loss, the expected direction for weaker dependency is more positive in the subgroup. These are not mechanistic claims: a threshold-sized interaction would indicate that the core associations are concentrated in particular assay conditions, while a null interaction supports that the accepted core map is not strongly diluted by these measured technical/contextual features in the supplied dataset. If any technical interaction shows a threshold-sized attenuation, later work should treat the corresponding core association as condition-sensitive rather than broadly robust within this dataset. All hypotheses remain dataset-specific associations and are falsifiable against the 0.15 composite dependency-score-unit threshold and the accompanying uncertainty.","analyze":"I selected the 10 currently untested registered claims H124-H133; these are all active empty-evidence claims, so they can yield new discovery results. Previously tested claims were avoided because rerunning them gives no new sample. The batch prioritizes PTEN context: H124 tests PTEN loss excluding MSI-high to assess whether the secondary PTEN signal survives when the very strong MSI-high predictor is removed, while H133 tests a stricter low-mutation-burden non-MSI background. H125 tests whether PTEN-loss dependency effects are modified by chromosomal instability. H126 is a locus-aware follow-up to unsupported MYC amplification, testing whether MYC-amplification effects are more consistent with a claimed stronger-dependency direction in high 8q24 copy-number backgrounds. The remaining six are diagnostic moderators of the accepted core map: high Cas9 activity (H127-H129) and adherent growth pattern (H130-H132) for SMARCA4 loss, KEAP1 loss, and TP53 loss. For direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates support stronger dependency in the exposed group or claimed amplification of the effect in the subgroup; for direction +1 claims, positive signed estimates support weaker dependency in the exposed group or claimed amplification in the subgroup. Interpretation will require effect magnitude and uncertainty around the 0.15-unit threshold, not just interval exclusion of zero.","appraise":"I interpreted all new signed estimates using the registered convention: for main effects with direction -1, a positive signed value means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive signed value means weaker dependency; for interactions, a positive signed value means the contrast is stronger in the subgroup than in the complement in the registered interaction direction. The PTEN-loss consolidation tests remain suggestive rather than individually conclusive. H117 tests PTEN loss in the common adenocarcinoma, KEAP1-intact, TP53-intact background and gives +0.225 (95% interval +0.124 to +0.326). The point estimate is above the 0.15-unit threshold, but the lower bound is not, and this is one of several correlated PTEN context tests; I keep it unresolved but defer it until the more focused pending validation result for H111 arrives. H118 tests PTEN loss among SMARCA4-loss, TP53-intact cells and gives +0.167 (95% +0.005 to +0.330). The point is just above threshold, but the interval is extremely wide, the exposed cell is only n=47, and the lower bound is far below threshold; this is best treated as an underpowered masking/falsification test, not as robust evidence. H119 tests PTEN loss among high mutation-burden cells and gives +0.204 (95% +0.060 to +0.347). For interactions, positive means the registered interaction direction is present. H124 tests PTEN loss among MSI-high-negative cells. It gives +0.2345 (95% +0.1382 to +0.3308; R131). The point estimate exceeds the 0.15-unit threshold and the sign is correct, but the lower bound remains just below threshold. Because this is the most direct remaining test of whether PTEN relevance survives removal of the very strong MSI-high predictor, I keep it unresolved and request independent validation rather than accept it. H133 tests PTEN loss among MSI-negative and low-mutation-burden cells and gives +0.2514 (+0.1211 to +0.3817; R132). It is concordant but less precise and also below threshold at the lower bound, so it supports the general PTEN context story but does not establish a threshold-sized effect; it is deferred. H125 tests whether PTEN-loss effects are amplified by high aneuploidy and gives -0.0029 (-0.1944 to +0.1886; R133). There is no evidence of the claimed interaction, so it is rejected and closed. H126 is invalid because one required cell has n=0, so the registered MYC-amplification-by-8q24 interaction cannot be evaluated as specified; I close it as unresolved rather than treating the invalid test as evidence against MYC biology. Technical moderators: H127, H128, and H129 test claimed amplification of core predictors in high-Cas9 cells. H127 gives -0.1701 (-0.3172 to -0.0230), which is opposite the claimed direction for SMARCA4-loss interaction. This is evidence of attenuation under high Cas9 activity rather than claimed amplification; I reject the registered H127 claim and do not promote the opposite direction to acceptance because it is post-hoc, multiple-tested, and a reversed interval would have lower bound only about +0.023. H128 gives -0.1427 (-0.2834 to -0.0021), again opposite the claimed direction and below threshold; reject and close. H129 gives -0.1155 (-0.3218 to +0.0908), null; reject and close. Adherent-growth moderators: H130 gives +0.0704 (-0.0718 to +0.2126), not supporting a threshold-sized SMARCA4 interaction; reject and close. H131 gives +0.1738 (+0.0180 to +0.3297), which is in the claimed KEAP1 direction and above threshold at the point estimate, but the lower bound is far below threshold and this is a post-hoc interaction screen; keep unresolved but deferred rather than accept. H132 gives +0.0392 (-0.1876 to +0.2660), null; reject and close. Overall, these new results do not establish a broad threshold-sized PTEN effect. They strengthen concordance of PTEN associations in non-MSI and low-TMB backgrounds but keep the conclusion context-dependent because lower confidence bounds remain below threshold. The core dataset-specific map remains: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency; TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss with much weaker dependency; MSI-high with much stronger dependency; PTEN loss is a secondary context-specific association.
