record.narrative: All newly delivered estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so a positive estimate supports the claimed association and acceptance requires a signed 95% lower bound above the 0.15 composite-unit threshold. The strongest threshold-robust new context tests are for the core associations: SMARCA4 loss in high-AXL expression cells has signed mean +0.8839 with lower +0.7902 (R192); KEAP1 loss in hypoxia-high cells has signed mean +0.8273 with lower +0.7359 (R193); TP53 loss in high-MYC-expression cells has signed mean +0.4480 with lower +0.3197 (R194); and MSI-high in high-MYC-expression cells has signed mean +0.7823 with lower +0.6175 despite a smaller exposed cell (R195). I accept H184-H187 and close them as further follow-up, because the core predictors already have stronger overall evidence and, in key cases, independent validation. These are presence-within-context association results in the supplied dataset, not formal effect-modification tests, causal knockout effects, or claims of external generalizability. The PTEN-loss context tests remain inconclusive. H179, H180, H181, H182, and H183 have favorable signed point estimates above the threshold, but their lower bounds are below 0.15 and are near zero: lower bounds +0.060, +0.098, +0.087, +0.133, and +0.119, respectively. The previously active high-ploidy PTEN test H178 had a lower bound below zero. Given that the overall PTEN-loss stronger-dependency claim is not threshold robust, that PTEN has been examined across many correlated contexts, and the independent validation budget is exhausted, accepting additional marginal PTEN subgroup contexts would carry substantial multiplicity and false-positive risk. I therefore retain the PTEN context results as unresolved uncertainty rather than evidence of null effect, and close these investigations. I close H178 for the same reason. The accepted dataset-specific map remains SMARCA4-loss associated with stronger composite dependency, TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss associated with weaker composite dependency, and MSI-high associated with stronger composite dependency, with PTEN loss secondary and context-dependent. To allocate remaining investigation without further PTEN subgroup mining, I registered completion of the serum-factor comparison set, 5% versus 2% and 10% versus 2%, because 10% versus 5% was already non-significant. These are dataset-specific main-effect checks rather than validation requests; no validation was possible because no new validation budget remains.

Iteration 16/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum

record.narrative: No new independent validation was delivered in this synthesis, no response deadline is open, and no assessments are due; the voluntary validation budget is exhausted. I therefore treated this stage as a dataset-specific synthesis rather than a request for further confirmatory evidence. The run has established a clear, threshold-robust association map for dependency_composite in the supplied dataset, using the 0.15 composite-unit absolute effect-size threshold. All numerical statements below use estimates and intervals already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so a signed lower bound above +0.15 was the acceptance criterion. More negative dependency_composite values denote stronger dependency; therefore accepted claims for TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss in the +1 direction mean weaker dependency, whereas accepted claims for SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high in the -1 direction mean stronger dependency. The endpoint is a composite dependency score, not a single-gene knockout phenotype, and all conclusions are associations in this supplied dataset, not causal gene-specific effects or externally validated biological generalizations. Supported findings. SMARCA4 loss is robustly associated with stronger composite dependency: overall signed discovery estimate +0.8325, 95% lower bound +0.7667, upper bound +0.8983, R5; independent validation signed estimate +0.7976, lower bound +0.6971, upper bound +0.8981, R13. This stronger-dependency association was also accepted in many measured strata and co-mutation backgrounds, including adenocarcinoma, adherent growth, high- and low-serum media, KY and non-KY library cells, matched and non-matched omics availability contexts, ploidy strata, and TP53-, KEAP1-, STK11-, ARID1A-, MSI-negative, and other backgrounds. These acceptance results establish presence within contexts, not formal effect modification. TP53 loss is robustly associated with weaker composite dependency: signed discovery estimate +0.4232, lower +0.3268, upper +0.5195, R2; independent validation signed estimate +0.3985, lower +0.2633, upper +0.5336, R39. Accepted contexts include adenocarcinoma, adherent growth, high-serum media, non-KY library cells, non-matched RNA-DNA cells, ploidy strata, and multiple co-mutation backgrounds. TP53-loss weaker-dependency associations were not threshold-robust in several low-power or searched contexts, including low-serum media R156, KY-library cells R158, MSI-high cells R180, and ARID1A-loss cells R174. These are unresolved uncertainty, not evidence of no effect. KEAP1 loss is robustly associated with weaker composite dependency: signed discovery estimate +0.8315, lower +0.7658, upper +0.8972, R4; independent validation signed estimate +0.7648, lower +0.6687, upper +0.8609, R92. Accepted contexts include adenocarcinoma, adherent growth, high- and low-serum media, KY and non-KY library cells, non-matched omics availability contexts, ploidy strata, and multiple co-mutation backgrounds. MSI-high status is robustly associated with stronger composite dependency: signed discovery estimate +0.7918, lower +0.6763, upper +0.9072, R56; independent validation signed estimate +0.7690, lower +0.5936, upper +0.9443, R78. Accepted contexts include many TP53-, KEAP1-, SMARCA4-, STK11-, mutation-burden, subtype, media, and library backgrounds. Secondary and unresolved finding. PTEN loss is context-dependent and not threshold-robust for a stronger-dependency claim overall: signed discovery estimate +0.2268, lower +0.1307, upper +0.3229, R20; independent validation signed estimate +0.1997, lower +0.0482, upper +0.3512, R119. It is accepted in several measured contexts, including TP53-intact, KEAP1-intact, KEAP1-loss, TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact, TP53-intact KEAP1-intact, TP53-intact SMARCA4-intact, adenocarcinoma TP53-intact SMARCA4-intact, and MSI-negative TP53/KEAP1-intact backgrounds. However, many PTEN-loss subgroup comparisons are favorable in point estimate but not threshold-robust, including STK11/TP53-intact contexts, MSI-negative overall contexts, high- and low-ploidy contexts, aneuploidy and expression-defined contexts, and low-power co-mutation backgrounds. Because PTEN has been examined across many correlated contexts and the independent validation budget is exhausted, I retain PTEN as a secondary association with unresolved context dependence rather than as a broad threshold-robust overall claim. Negative findings. The dataset-specific evidence does not support scientifically meaningful dependency_composite differences for KRAS mutation R1, STK11 loss main effect R3, MYC amplification main effect R6, PIK3CA mutation R38, ARID1A loss main effect R17, MTAP loss main effect and MTAP-loss in CDKN2A-loss cells R18, R79, R154, RB1 loss R21, SMAD4 loss R22, NF1 loss R57, BRCA2 loss R55, BRAF V600E R59, EGFR amplification R60 and R106, ERBB2 amplification R61, APC mutation R58 and R128, research marker D, E, and F positivity R7, R8, R54, omics-availability indicators R28, R77, R76, CRISPR-library main effects R9, R62, R75, the tested media-serum 10 versus 5 contrast R63, and batch_a versus batch_b R115. CDKN2A loss as a stronger-dependency claim had a favorable signed estimate R19 but its lower bound was below threshold. Many formal interaction tests were rejected or invalid, so the dataset supports presence of core associations across many strata but does not support reliable effect modification. Unresolved uncertainty. The main unresolved areas are low-power or repeatedly searched contexts: TP53-loss in low-serum media, KY-library cells, MSI-high cells, and ARID1A-loss cells; PTEN-loss in many borderline subgroups; MYC-amplification interaction with MYC expression and copy-number-defined MYC contexts; KEAP1 interaction by adherent growth; and some CDKN2A secondary effects. Closing these investigations is a resource allocation decision, not a claim that their point estimates are null. Next analysis. The most informative next discovery analyses are the newly registered media-serum 2% contexts for the four core predictors: TP53 loss, SMARCA4 loss, KEAP1 loss, and MSI-high. These complete the serum-level robustness check for the core association map and test whether the already validated associations remain threshold-robust in the lowest serum condition. The active registered serum main effects H188 and H189, 5% versus 2% and 10% versus 2%, will also be evaluated. If any media-serum 2% context is threshold-robust, it will add a new robust serum context to the core findings; if underpowered or non-threshold-robust, it should be retained as unresolved technical context dependence and not used to weaken the supported overall associations. No validation can be requested because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so further inferences must remain dataset-specific and cautious.

prompt:
Iteration 17/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due and the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so the next useful comparisons are targeted discovery analyses in a biologically motivated but not fully resolved context: MYC amplification and MYC expression. The strongest supported dataset-specific association map remains SMARCA4 loss with stronger composite dependency, TP53 loss with weaker composite dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker composite dependency, and MSI-high status with stronger composite dependency. PTEN loss remains secondary and context-dependent. I intentionally avoid additional PTEN subgroup mining because PTEN has already been examined across many correlated contexts and the lower bounds are borderline; accepting more marginal PTEN contexts would risk multiplicity without a new independent confirmatory budget.

The first proposal refines the unresolved MYC-amplification interaction by expression (H78/R129). H78 was a formal interaction, so it tested whether the MYC-amplification contrast differs between high- and low-MYC-expression cells, and it was favorable but not threshold-robust. This new proposal asks a simpler and falsifiable question: within cells with high MYC expression, is MYC amplification associated with a threshold-robust stronger dependency relative to MYC-intact cells? The claim direction is -1 because more negative dependency_composite means stronger dependency. If MYC amplification matters primarily when MYC transcript abundance is high, the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast should be negative, and the signed estimate should have a lower bound above +0.15 composite units. Alternatives include no threshold-robust effect in high-expression cells, a stronger-dependency effect not confined to expression, or an opposite weaker-dependency association.

The remaining proposals test the core dependency predictors inside the genomic MYC-amplification stratum. MYC amplification is a measured predictor that could indicate proliferative or transcriptional stress, and it may modify or preserve dependencies on chromatin remodeling, p53 pathway loss, and oxidative-stress/NRF2-associated biology. These are context-persistence tests, not formal interaction tests: each compares exposed versus comparator only among MYC-amplified cells. SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA4-intact cells is tested with direction -1, expecting that SMARCA4 loss remains associated with stronger dependency in MYC-amplified cells; plausible alternatives are attenuation toward null or reversal. TP53-loss versus TP53-intact cells is tested with direction +1, expecting that TP53 loss remains associated with weaker dependency, i.e., less negative composite scores, in MYC-amplified cells; alternatives include attenuation or reversal, especially if MYC amplification creates synthetic-lethal-like conditions that strengthen dependency despite TP53 loss. KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-intact cells is tested with direction +1, expecting that KEAP1 loss remains associated with weaker dependency, with alternatives of attenuation or reversal.

All returned estimates and intervals will already be signed to the registered hypothesis direction. In appraise, acceptance will require a signed 95% lower bound above +0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction; favorable point estimates with lower bounds below that threshold will remain unresolved, and estimates not favoring the claimed direction will be rejected. These analyses remain associations within the supplied composite dependency dataset. They are not causal knockout claims, not single-gene knockout phenotypes, and not claims of external biological generalizability. They do not consume validation budget and are designed to resolve a specific unresolved MYC-expression question while adding informative context robustness for the core predictors.

PTEN loss remains secondary and context-dependent. I intentionally avoid additional PTEN subgroup mining because PTEN has already been examined across many correlated contexts and the lower bounds are borderline; accepting more marginal PTEN contexts would risk multiplicity without a new independent confirmatory budget.\n\nThe first proposal refines the unresolved MYC-amplification interaction by expression (H78/R129). H78 was a formal interaction, so it tested whether the MYC-amplification contrast differs between high- and low-MYC-expression cells, and it was favorable but not threshold-robust. This new proposal asks a simpler and falsifiable question: within cells with high MYC expression, is MYC amplification associated with a threshold-robust stronger dependency relative to MYC-intact cells? The claim direction is -1 because more negative dependency_composite means stronger dependency. If MYC amplification matters primarily when MYC transcript abundance is high, the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast should be negative, and the signed estimate should have a lower bound above +0.15 composite units. Alternatives include no threshold-robust effect in high-expression cells, a stronger-dependency effect not confined to expression, or an opposite weaker-dependency association.\n\nThe remaining proposals test the core dependency predictors inside the genomic MYC-amplification stratum. MYC amplification is a measured predictor that could indicate proliferative or transcriptional stress, and it may modify or preserve dependencies on chromatin remodeling, p53 pathway loss, and oxidative-stress/NRF2-associated biology. These are context-persistence tests, not formal interaction tests: each compares exposed versus comparator only among MYC-amplified cells. SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA4-intact cells is tested with direction -1, expecting that SMARCA4 loss remains associated with stronger dependency in MYC-amplified cells; plausible alternatives are attenuation toward null or reversal. TP53-loss versus TP53-intact cells is tested with direction +1, expecting that TP53 loss remains associated with weaker dependency, i.e., less negative composite scores, in MYC-amplified cells; alternatives include attenuation or reversal, especially if MYC amplification creates synthetic-lethal-like conditions that strengthen dependency despite TP53 loss. KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-intact cells is tested with direction +1, expecting that KEAP1 loss remains associated with weaker dependency, with alternatives of attenuation or reversal.\n\nAll returned estimates and intervals will already be signed to the registered hypothesis direction. In appraise, acceptance will require a signed 95% lower bound above +0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction; favorable point estimates with lower bounds below that threshold will remain unresolved, and estimates not favoring the claimed direction will be rejected. These analyses remain associations within the supplied composite dependency dataset. They are not causal knockout claims, not single-gene knockout phenotypes, and not claims of external biological generalizability. prompt:
Iteration 17/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
All new estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so I evaluated them against the 0.15 composite-unit threshold using the signed 95% lower bound. The serum main-effect completions are negative for the registered positive direction: H188 (5% versus 2%, R196) has signed estimate +0.010, lower bound -0.088, and H189 (10% versus 2%, R197) has signed estimate +0.012, lower bound -0.072. Both point estimates are far below the threshold and their intervals include zero, so I reject these meaningful weaker-dependency claims and close them. The serum context tests for the core predictors are threshold-robust: TP53 loss at 2% serum is associated with weaker dependency (+0.424, lower +0.190; H190/R198); SMARCA4 loss at 2% serum is associated with stronger dependency (+0.848, lower +0.680; H191/R199); KEAP1 loss at 2% serum is associated with weaker dependency (+0.910, lower +0.754; H192/R200); and MSI-high at 2% serum is associated with stronger dependency (+0.743, lower +0.503; H193/R201). I accept all four as dataset-specific presence-in-context associations and close them. H193 has a small exposed cell (n=24), but it satisfies the prespecified 20-per-cell rule and its interval remains well above threshold; nonetheless it should not be overinterpreted as a new overall effect because the overall MSI-high claim was independently validated earlier.

The focused MYC follow-up is mixed. The direct test of MYC amplification among high-MYC-expression cells (H194/R202) has signed estimate +0.063, lower bound -0.033, upper bound +0.159. It does not support a threshold-robust stronger-dependency association, so I reject and close H194. This does not directly resolve the earlier formal interaction claim H78, which remains a separate question; H194 simply fails to show the simpler mean difference that motivated it. By contrast, the three core predictors remain threshold-robust within the MYC-amplification stratum: SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger dependency (+0.791, lower +0.636; H195/R203); TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency (+0.676, lower +0.443; H196/R204); and KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker dependency (+0.901, lower +0.725; H197/R205). I accept these as context-persistence results, not formal effect-modification or causal claims. They are marginal within-stratum comparisons and may be influenced by correlated co-mutations or screen features, but their lower bounds are far above the effect-size threshold.

Independent validation is not possible because no new validation requests remain, and none are needed to change the status of these context results: the overall SMARCA4, TP53, KEAP1, and MSI-high claims already have prior independent validation, while these new analyses only test whether the associations persist in specified dataset contexts. I close these investigations because further subgroup mining would add multiplicity risk, especially for PTEN and marginal MYC contexts, without additional confirmatory capacity.

prompt:
Iteration 17/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative:
No new independent validation was delivered at this synthesis and no response deadline is open; assessments_due is empty. I nonetheless reviewed PTEN-loss claims with available validation evidence. H111, PTEN loss versus PTEN intact in STK11-loss/TP53-loss-intact cells, had signed discovery estimate +0.235 with lower bound +0.136 (R109) and signed validation estimate +0.263 with lower bound +0.105 (R130). Both point estimates exceed the 0.15 composite-unit threshold, but neither lower bound does; therefore this remains unresolved. H124, PTEN loss versus PTEN intact in MSI-negative cells, had signed discovery estimate +0.234 with lower bound +0.138 (R131) and signed validation estimate +0.280 with lower bound +0.141 (R141), again favorable but below the threshold for robust claim acceptance. The overall PTEN-loss stronger-dependency refinement H32 also remains unresolved: signed discovery lower bound +0.131 (R20) and validation lower bound +0.048 (R119). These reassessments do not change the accepted claim set; they sharpen that PTEN loss is a secondary context-dependent signal rather than a broadly threshold-robust overall effect.

The main supported dataset-specific findings are four core composite-dependency associations. More negative dependency_composite values mean stronger dependency; all signed estimates and intervals below are already oriented to the claimed hypothesis direction, so a signed lower bound above +0.15 was treated as evidence for a scientifically meaningful effect. SMARCA4 loss is robustly associated with stronger composite dependency: signed overall discovery estimate +0.8325, 95% lower bound +0.7667 to +0.8983 (R5), and independent validation estimate +0.7976, lower bound +0.6971 to +0.8981 (R13). TP53 loss is robustly associated with weaker composite dependency: signed overall discovery estimate +0.4232, lower bound +0.3268 to +0.5195 (R2), and independent validation estimate +0.3985, lower bound +0.2633 to +0.5336 (R39); the opposite stronger-dependency claim H2 was rejected. KEAP1 loss is robustly associated with weaker composite dependency: signed overall discovery estimate +0.8315, lower bound +0.7658 to +0.8972 (R4), and independent validation estimate +0.7648, lower bound +0.6687 to +0.8609 (R92); the opposite stronger-dependency claim H4 was rejected. MSI-high status is robustly associated with stronger composite dependency: signed overall discovery estimate +0.7918, lower bound +0.6763 to +0.9072 (R56), and independent validation estimate +0.7690, lower bound +0.5936 to +0.9443 (R78). These conclusions are associations with measured predictor status within the supplied composite-dependency dataset, not causal single-gene knockout effects, and not external biological generalization claims.

The core map is also context-presistent across many measured strata. In the newly assessed 2% serum context, TP53 loss remained associated with weaker dependency (+0.424, lower +0.190; R198), SMARCA4 loss with stronger dependency (+0.848, lower +0.680; R199), KEAP1 loss with weaker dependency (+0.910, lower +0.754; R200), and MSI-high with stronger dependency (+0.743, lower +0.503; R201). Within MYC-amplification cells, the same core predictors remained threshold-robust: SMARCA4 loss stronger (+0.791, lower +0.636; R203), TP53 loss weaker (+0.676, lower +0.443; R204), and KEAP1 loss weaker (+0.901, lower +0.725; R205). These are context presence tests, not formal effect-modification claims.

PTEN loss remains the main secondary signal. Several measured PTEN-loss contexts are accepted, including TP53-intact cells (R34 with validation R53), KEAP1-intact cells (R35 with validation R105), KEAP1-loss cells (R51), TP53/KEAP1-intact cells (R49), MSI-negative TP53/KEAP1-intact cells (R142), and TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact cells (R151). However, the overall PTEN-loss claim and several key borderline contexts, including H32, H111, and H124, do not have lower bounds above the 0.15 threshold. Because PTEN has been examined across many correlated co-mutation and molecular contexts and the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, I retain PTEN loss as a secondary association with unresolved context dependence rather than promoting it to a broad threshold-robust overall claim.

Negative dataset-specific findings include no scientifically meaningful dependency_composite differences for KRAS mutation (R1), STK11 main effect (R3), MYC amplification main effect (R6), PIK3CA mutation (R38), ARID1A main effect (R17), MTAP main effect and MTAP in CDKN2A-loss cells (R18, R79, R154), RB1 loss (R21), SMAD4 loss (R22), NF1 loss (R57), BRCA2 loss (R55), BRAF V600E (R59), EGFR amplification (R60, R106), ERBB2 amplification (R61), APC mutation and APC interaction by WNT activity (R58, R128), research markers D/E/F positivity (R7, R8, R54), omics-availability indicators (R28, R77, R76), CRISPR-library main effects (R9, R62, R75), media-serum main-effect contrasts (R63, R196, R197), and screen batch (R115). CDKN2A loss is not a broadly accepted stronger-dependency effect; its favorable main effect R19 had lower bound +0.062, and most subgroup or interaction contexts were unresolved or rejected. MYC amplification among high-MYC-expression cells was near null and rejected (R202), although the direct formal MYC-by-MYC-expression interaction H78 remains a separate unresolved interaction question. Most formal interaction tests, including co-mutation, lineage, growth, screen-QC, Cas9, expression, ploidy, aneuploidy, and mutation-burden modifiers, were rejected or invalid. The dataset therefore supports robust presence of core associations across many strata more than it supports reliable effect modification.

Unresolved uncertainty is concentrated in low-power or repeatedly searched contexts: PTEN-loss in STK11/TP53-intact cells (H111), MSI-negative cells (H124), and overall (H32); TP53-loss in low-serum media (H148), KY-library cells (H151), ARID1A-loss cells (H166), and MSI-high cells (H172); MYC-amplification interaction with expression and copy-number-defined MYC contexts; KEAP1 interaction by adherent growth; and some CDKN2A secondary effects. Closing these investigations is a resource-allocation and multiplicity-control decision, not evidence that their point estimates are null.

No new validation can be requested because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, and no new proposals are registered now because further subgroup mining would mainly add multiplicity risk without independent confirmation. If confirmatory capacity were available, the most informative next analyses would be targeted independent validation of the borderline PTEN contexts H111 and H124, low-power TP53-loss contexts H148, H151, H166, and H172, and a pre-specified joint assessment of the core SMARCA4, TP53, KEAP1, and MSI effects with strict control of multiplicity. For now, the defensible conclusion is a dataset-specific association map: SMARCA4 loss with stronger composite dependency, TP53 loss with weaker composite dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker composite dependency, and MSI-high with stronger composite dependency, while PTEN loss remains secondary and context-dependent.

prompt:
Iteration 18/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

record.narrative: No assessments are due and no new voluntary validation request is possible, so this stage registers only discovery comparisons. I continue from the dataset-specific core map: SMARCA4 loss associated with stronger composite dependency, TP53 loss associated with weaker composite dependency, KEAP1 loss associated with weaker composite dependency, and MSI-high associated with stronger composite dependency. I deliberately avoid further PTEN-loss subgroup mining because PTEN has already been examined across many correlated contexts, several lower bounds remain below the 0.15 composite-unit threshold, and no confirmatory validation budget remains. The first four new claims test whether constructed research signature A modifies each robust core predictor. The signature A subgroup is defined as above the median to keep cell counts adequate. For SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high, the hypothesis is that high signature A increases the stronger-dependency association, so the raw interaction is expected negative and the registered claim direction is -1. For KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss, the hypothesis is that high signature A increases the weaker-dependency association, so the raw interaction is expected positive and the registered claim direction is +1. Plausible alternatives for all four are no threshold-robust effect modification or an opposite modification. The next two claims extend the SMARCA4-by-signature question to signature B and signature C, using median splits and the same expected stronger-dependency interaction direction because SMARCA4 loss is the strongest core signal. The marker-D proposal asks a context-specific synthetic-like question: among SMARCA4-loss cells, is research marker D positivity associated with stronger dependency, raw negative, direction -1. This refines the overall marker-D null rather than repeating it. The sex proposal tests a measured demographic contrast, male versus female, with a tentative expectation of male weaker dependency, raw positive, direction +1; alternatives include no sex difference or female weaker dependency. The batch proposal tests an additional screen batch, batch_c versus batch_a, primarily as a measurement-homogeneity check, with uncertain expected direction. In appraise, I will accept only if the signed 95% lower bound exceeds +0.15 composite dependency-score units in the registered direction; favorable estimates with lower bounds below +0.15 will remain unresolved, and unfavorable estimates will be rejected. These proposals remain dataset-specific associations with measured predictors and constructed assays, not causal single-gene knockout effects or external biological claims.

prompt:
Iteration 18/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

prompt:
Iteration 18/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.
